extracted.intended_audience: R package authors, contributors, and prospective volunteer reviewers (rOpenSci community)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and policies for submitting R packages to rOpenSci's open, GitHub-based software peer review system and for volunteering as reviewers or editors. Describes process norms, responsibilities, artifacts (badges, docs), and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent, constructive, non-adversarial, open review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages contributed by the community undergo a transparent, constructive, non adversarial and open review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are public conversations intended to be non-adversarial and focused on improving software quality. The process aims to provide useful feedback to authors and to be open so the broader community can observe and participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two external reviews per submission
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two external reviews as important milestones for each submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review process is an ongoing conversation until acceptance of the package, with two external reviews marking key points in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers examine software code and user experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers (two per submission) examine the software code and user experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews focus on improving software quality by assessing code, documentation, user-facing behavior, and overall usability. Feedback should be constructive and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use GitHub issues as the technical review platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Each package review process is an issue in the ropensci/software-review GitHub repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review is conducted as an issue thread (ongoing conversation). Example: the ropenaq package review thread. GitHub features such as issue templates (used as submission templates) and labels are used to manage and track review progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of issue templates and labels to track progress
rubrics_metrics.description: We use GitHub features such as issue templates (as submission templates), and labelling which we use to track progress of submissions (from editor checks to approval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow the submission template when creating the review issue. Editors and maintainers apply labels to indicate stages (e.g., editor checks, review in progress, approval).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open review with identities known and public threads
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing threads are public. Authors, reviewers, and editors all know each other’s identities. The broader community can view or even participate in the conversation as it happens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Openness incentivizes thorough, non-adversarial reviews and community building. The page acknowledges potential drawbacks (e.g., possible bias compared to double-blind review, reviewers being less critical) but argues openness provides checks on unsupported or subjective comments. Authors and reviewers may contact editors privately if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate editors manage incoming flow and ensure progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Associate editors manage the incoming flow and ensure progress of submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associate editors coordinate reviews, assign reviewers, and track the submission from initial checks to acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-reviewed badge and links in README and packages page
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci packages that have been peer-reviewed are recognized via a green “peer-reviewed” badge in their README and via a blue comment icon near their description on the rOpenSci packages page, both linking to their reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should include the badge in their README to signal review status. The linked review thread provides transparency on review history and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docs website automatically built and deployable
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages in the rOpenSci suite get a documentation website that is automatically built and deployed after each push (docs.ropensci.org).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can link this docs site from their DESCRIPTION. rOpenSci helps host and build documentation as part of the reviewed package benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors retain ownership and receive maintenance support
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors retain ownership and control of their package, but rOpenSci can help with ongoing maintenance issues such as those associated with updates to R and dependencies and CRAN policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting does not transfer ownership by default; rOpenSci offers assistance for maintenance and compatibility over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and visibility benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci will promote your package through our webpage, blog, and social media (e.g., Mastodon, LinkedIn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewed packages may be featured on rOpenSci channels. rOpenSci will also promote gitbooks related to your package if provided and can transfer book sources to ropensci-books for listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-listing with other repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci packages can be cross-listed with other repositories such as CRAN and BioConductor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are free to list their package on other appropriate repositories in addition to rOpenSci.

rubrics_metrics.name: JOSS fast-track eligibility for in-scope packages
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci packages that are in scope for the Journal of Open-Source Software (JOSS) and add the necessary accompanying short paper may, at the discretion of JOSS editors, benefit from a fast-tracked review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors submit the short paper required by JOSS and their package fits JOSS scope, they may be eligible for expedited handling by JOSS editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to transfer repository to rOpenSci organization
rubrics_metrics.description: If desired, your package repository may be transferred to the rOpenSci organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who prefer can move repository ownership to rOpenSci; transfer is optional and done with authors' consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional listing of reviewers in DESCRIPTION metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers agree to be listed in DESCRIPTION, their metadata will mention the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers can opt in to be credited in package metadata; authors may include reviewer metadata in DESCRIPTION to acknowledge contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer reviewer recruitment and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci solicits volunteer reviewers; reviewers give back to the community, learn development practices, and network with peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To volunteer, fill out a short form providing contact information and areas of expertise. rOpenSci seeks reviewers with general package-writing experience and domain expertise in fields where packages are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of open review trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Open review has potential drawbacks (e.g., non-blind reviews may affect representation or reviewer criticality) but is believed to improve fairness and quality by making comments public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors acknowledge research showing double-blind review can increase representation of female authors, and encourage private contact with editors when concerns arise. The public nature is framed as a check against unsupported comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial structure and rotation
rubrics_metrics.description: The software peer review process is run by an Editor-in-Chief (rotated generally every three months), an editorial team, and volunteer reviewers; current team and status are available on an interactive dashboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rotating Editor-in-Chief and named editorial team members manage policy and operations; authors and reviewers can consult the dashboard for current staff and review status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution when reusing rOpenSci standards/checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use rOpenSci standards/checklists when reviewing software elsewhere, attribute that they came from rOpenSci and tell rOpenSci (public forum or private email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying rOpenSci materials in other review contexts (journals, classrooms, internal reviews), acknowledge the source and optionally notify rOpenSci.
